subject: Microburst aggregation charge — request for breakdown
messages:
From: Olivia Klein <olivia.k@blueharbor.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Blue Harbor Finance <finance@blueharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle microburst charges — need breakdown

Hi Mina,

We noticed three small line items on the April invoice that together pushed us into an overage band. The amounts are small individually (~$12–$18 each) but appear repeatedly across a 48-hour window on Apr 17–18 and resulted in a surprise charge of ~$540.

Attached is a CSV export from our side (2027-04-usage-microbursts.csv) with timestamps and request IDs; you can see many calls that are <2s in duration but show non-trivial token consumption. Can you confirm how your metering treats very short streaming sessions — are they aggregated into a single session for billing or counted separately? We suspect sub-second handoffs between our frontend and background worker may be creating separate billable sessions.

We'd appreciate a cleaned usage export (per-request token counts and aggregation keys) and a provisional credit while you investigate — our procurement team is holding the payment until we understand the variance. Please loop in billing ops.

Thanks,
Olivia Klein
Head of Integrations, Blue Harbor Health
olivia.k@blueharbor.com
+1 415-555-8273

(Attachment: 2027-04-usage-microbursts.csv)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Klein <olivia.k@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle microburst charges — need breakdown

Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick flag and the CSV. I've looped in Marcus from Billing and Laura from Finance Ops to pull the per-request usage log and audit the aggregation keys.

Quick note: we do merge requests server-side when they land on the same router with matching cache keys, but very short-lived connections can sometimes create separate consumer sessions depending on the SDK/edge retry behavior. We'll send a short export with raw token counts + aggregation id for the April 17–18 window within the hour.

I'll also ask Marcus to propose a provisional credit so your procurement team can continue processing the payment.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Klein <olivia.k@blueharbor.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle microburst charges — need breakdown

Hello Olivia — I pulled the raw per-request export for Blue Harbor for 2027-04-17 to 2027-04-18 and attached a filtered CSV (2027-04-usage-microbursts.csv). Key findings: 

- There are 43 distinct request IDs in your CSV that we match to 47 server-side request entries (4 short-lived retries with different router UUIDs).
- Metering rule: each server-side request entry is billed separately; we only collapse entries when they share the same aggregation_id and contiguous token window. Short-lived handoffs where the client reconnects create separate entries.
- Many of your events are streaming start/stop pairs where the client closed the websocket and immediately reopened; those were counted as separate billable requests because the aggregation_id differed.
- Token breakdown (sample): request 8b7f — prompt 42 tokens, completion 318 tokens; request 8b7g (retry) — prompt 0, completion 12 tokens. We include the sample rows in the attached CSV.

Proposal to resolve quickly: we can apply a provisional credit equal to 75% of the disputed line items (~$405) while we run a full audit for duplicate short-lived routers and SDK-level retry deduping. If the audit shows system behavior that caused double-counting on our side we'll issue a full refund/credit and update your April invoice. If the audit confirms client-side retries as cause, we'll keep the 25% to cover valid consumption but provide guidance to reduce retries and suggest using our sticky-routing SDK flag to reduce router UUID churn.

I've attached: 1) the server-side filtered export, 2) draft invoice_2027-04-draft.pdf with a proposed provisional credit line, and 3) provisional_credit_form.pdf to sign if you accept the provisional credit.

Let me know if this provisional amount is acceptable and we'll queue the credit and adjust the invoice.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
(Attachments: 2027-04-usage-microbursts.csv, invoice_2027-04-draft.pdf, provisional_credit_form.pdf)

From: Olivia Klein <olivia.k@blueharbor.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Blue Harbor Finance <finance@blueharbor.com>, Craig Hartman <craig.h@blueharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Microburst aggregation charge — request for breakdown

Marcus — thanks for the fast investigation and the sample rows. The server-side CSV helps a lot. A few clarifying questions before we sign the provisional_credit_form: 

1) VAT handling: Blue Harbor is in the EU for VAT purposes — will the provisional credit be applied net-of-VAT or will we need a corrected invoice showing the VAT adjustment?
2) If we sign the provisional credit form now, can you guarantee the disputed charge will be on hold and not sent to collections while the audit completes?
3) What timeline do you have for the full audit and final resolution?

Our CFO Craig is on copy. We can sign the provisional form if the VAT handling and hold are confirmed. We prefer a corrected invoice showing the credit applied with VAT recalculated.

Best,
Olivia
(Attachment: none)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Blue Harbor Finance <finance@blueharbor.com>, Olivia Klein <olivia.k@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Microburst aggregation charge — request for breakdown

Hi Olivia / Craig — Laura here from Finance Ops. Quick answers: 

1) VAT: provisional credits are applied to the invoice gross; we will issue a corrected invoice that reflects the credit and the recalculated VAT amount (so you'll receive an invoice_net and an invoice_gross that matches your EU VAT requirements).
2) Hold: yes — we will place invoice BH-7462 on hold for 14 days while the audit completes; no collections actions will be taken in that window.
3) Timeline: Marcus' team will complete the technical audit within 5 business days; Finance Ops will generate the corrected invoice within 2 business days after the audit completes. If the audit clears a platform fault we will issue the full refund/credit; if client-side retries are confirmed we'll keep the agreed 25% and document the root cause and mitigation steps.

Next steps: Marcus will mark the provisional credit in our billing system today and share the DocuSign link for the provisional_credit_form.pdf. Once we receive the signed form we'll queue the hold and create a draft corrected invoice for your review.

Laura Bennett
Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
(Attachment: none)
